test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question: The average of n numbers is 45. If 60% of the numbers are increased by 5 each and the remaining numbers are decreased by 10 each, then what is the average of the numbers so obtained?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net deviation in average = (Percentage₁ × Change₁) + (Percentage₂ × Change₂)

Net deviation = (60% × +5) + (40% × −10)

Net deviation = 3 − 4 = −1

New Average = Old Average + Net deviation = 45 − 1 = 44

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of n numbers = 45

Group 1 = 60% of n, increase = +5 per number

Group 2 = 40% of n, decrease = −10 per number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9064ec408427c0faf17fafb2d5453dcc15064fe634e101131b1a3499bdc5c418.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total count of numbers (n) be 100.

⇒ Initial sum of n numbers = n × Average = 100 × 45 = 4500

⇒ Number of elements in 60% group = 0.60 × 100 = 60

⇒ Total increase in sum for this group = 60 × 5 = 300

⇒ Number of elements in remaining 40% group = 0.40 × 100 = 40

⇒ Total decrease in sum for this group = 40 × 10 = 400

⇒ New total sum = 4500 + 300 − 400 = 4400

⇒ New Average = New sum ÷ n = 4400 ÷ 100 = 44

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When a group is divided into parts with different averages or changes, the overall change is given by (n₁×c₁ + n₂×c₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Effect of Uniform Change

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the average of the set also increases or decreases by exactly 'k'.

Deviation Method

The new average can always be calculated as Old Average + (Net Sum of Deviations ÷ Total Count).</p
